messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Telugu, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Telugu line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
నేను అతనిని మహా ఎడారిలో చూసినప్పుడు, అతనికి నేను నన్ను కరుణించు అని అరిచాను, నీవు ఏవైనా నీడ లేదా నిజమైన మనిషి అయినా!

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Source → Telugu)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Quando | “when” (temporal subordinator) | **చూసినప్పుడు** | “when (I) saw” | OK | | vidi | “saw” (past‑tense verb) | **చూసిన** | “saw” | OK | | costui | demonstrative “this man” | **అతనిని** | “him” (acc.) | OK | | nel | “in the” (prep + article) | **లో** | “in” | OK | | gran | “great, large” (adj.) | **మహా** | “great” | OK | | diserto | “desert” (noun) | **ఎడారి** | “desert” | OK | | «Miserere | imperative “have pity” | **కరుణించు** | “have mercy” | OK | | di | preposition “of / on” (part of *di me*) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (Telugu marks the object with case ending) | | me» | pronoun “me” (acc.) | **నన్ను** | “me” | OK | | gridi | “I cried / shouted” (past) | **అరిచాను** | “I shouted” | OK | | a | preposition “to” (dative) | **కు** | “to” | OK | | lui, | pronoun “him” (dative) | **అతనికి** | “to him” | OK | | «qual | “whatever” (free‑relative) | **ఏవైనా** | “whatever” | OK | | che | relative particle (linker) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (no separate word in Telugu) | | tu | second‑person pronoun “you” | **నీవు** | “you” | OK | | sii, | subjunctive “be” (non‑assertive) | **అయినా** | “be (if/though)” | OK | | od (1) | disjunction “or” | **లేదా** | “or” | OK | | ombra | “shade, shadow” (noun) | **నీడ** | “shade” | OK | | od (2) | disjunction “or” | **లేదా** | “or” | OK | | omo | “man, human” (noun) | **మనిషి** | “man” | OK | | certo! | “certain, real” (adj.) | **నిజమైన** | “real / genuine” | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `di` (preposition) – Telugu expresses the object with the accusative suffix **‑ను** on *నన్ను*, so a separate preposition is not needed. - **UNNECESSARY**: `che` – the relative particle has no lexical counterpart in Telugu; the clause is linked implicitly.
All other source tokens are represented correctly, with appropriate grammatical agreement in the Telugu rendering.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Telugu script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
